PullRequest.Title: Refine chat session indicators and add topology telemetry
PullRequest.Body:
Follow-up to #332799 and #333253.

## State indicator feedback

- Removes the outer green frame while a request is running; the existing chat input progress border remains unchanged.
- Uses a green dotted one-stroke frame for an idle completion that has not been visited.
- Keeps the red dashed needs-input frame.
- Treats retained DOM focus as visited only while the owning window is focused, and recomputes on window focus/blur.
- Preserves a synchronous request-start edge when an accumulated add/complete batch is delivered after the model is already idle.
- Uses the same pending-aware idle rule as window notifications, including canceled/error-stranded queues.
- Relies on the effective `.monaco-reduce-motion` state instead of overriding it with a local OS media query.
- Clarifies the experimental setting description to match the states it now indicates.

## Chat Editor topology telemetry

Adds the count-only `chat.editorTopology` event after main-editor restoration and on coalesced topology changes involving Chat Editors:

- `openChatEditorCount`
- `visibleChatEditorCount`
- `chatEditorGroupCount`
- `visibleEditorCount`
- `editorGroupCount`

The event excludes dedicated Agents windows, is scoped to the main editor part, suppresses identical snapshots, and collects no session IDs, resources, titles, prompts, or content.

## Validation

- Targeted ESLint and telemetry classification checks
- Targeted stylelint
- `npm run compile-client`
- ChatWidget, ChatWindowNotifier, and ChatEditorTopologyTelemetry unit tests
- Staged-file hygiene
- Live Code OSS validation of running and unvisited visual states

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore the main editor area and open, close, activate, or rearrange editor tabs while Chat Editors may be present
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After main editor restoration, the contribution synchronously computes one initial topology snapshot. Later editor/group events only schedule a 100 ms timer; the O(open tabs) scan and telemetry dispatch run on that timer rather than inline with the triggering editor operation, though the timer callback itself runs on the renderer thread.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Desktop telemetry logging sends the count-only snapshot to the shared-process telemetry appender; web telemetry uses its asynchronous appender instead.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one dispatch per 100 ms event burst, and only when the five-count snapshot differs and either the current or previous snapshot contains an open Chat Editor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No chat editor topology scan or chat.editorTopology telemetry dispatch existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The publicLog2 call performs synchronous data cleaning/mixing before handing off to the asynchronous appender, but does not await IPC/network completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The snapshot scan is O(G + N), where G is main editor groups and N is total open tabs across those groups; each scan allocates one group object and one type-id array per group, plus filter results. RunOnceScheduler coalesces all events in a 100 ms window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single RunOnceScheduler serializes/coalesces topology recomputation. Telemetry IPC promises are not awaited, but dispatch occurs only for distinct qualifying snapshots.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The previous five-count snapshot is cached. Identical warm snapshots suppress telemetry, but the collection scan is still required to establish equality. Cold startup performs one scan and logs only if a Chat Editor is open.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the O(N) scan, allocation shape, timer placement, deduplication, and desktop IPC path from the changed code and telemetry implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users can have hundreds of open tabs, but the linear operations are simple property reads and small temporary arrays, editor changes are interaction-driven, and bursts are coalesced; no evidence establishes material latency or CPU pressure.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: this introduces measurable work, but coalescing, count-snapshot deduplication, asynchronous dispatch, and realistic editor-event frequency keep it below the actionable performance threshold.

Scenarios.Scenario: Stream, queue, complete, cancel, or error a chat request while the session-state indicator is enabled or disabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Accumulated ChatViewModel changes synchronously update progress and session-indicator classes. The new idle calculation reads request flags, the last response, and the pending queue length before class toggles; pending-queue changes invoke the same O(1) indicator update directly.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work scales with accumulated model-change callbacks and the number of live ChatWidget instances bound to the model. getPendingRequests returns the existing array, so checking length is O(1) and does not copy the queue.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Updates run serially on the UI thread. View-model events are already accumulated; pending-queue mutations emit one event per queue operation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is needed for the constant-time state read. ClassList.toggle receives the computed state on each callback and browser style work is limited to each live widget.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from ChatModel.getPendingRequests returning its backing array and the ChatWidget subscription/call flow.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact model event rates vary during streaming, but the added state reads are constant-time and the widget already performed DOM class updates on this path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff adds constant-time queue/response checks and infrequent window focus listeners, not scaling queue traversal or new external I/O.

Scenarios.Scenario: Show request progress and unvisited/needs-input visual states in Chat Editors
Scenarios.CriticalPath: During an active request, the input progress-border CSS animation renders continuously when enabled and motion is not reduced. The diff removes the previous whole-widget animated box-shadow state and allows the existing input-border animation to remain active when the experimental session indicator is enabled.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Rendering cost scales with the number of simultaneously visible live ChatWidgets with active requests; ChatEditor owns one widget per instantiated editor pane/group rather than one per inactive tab.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser rendering schedules the CSS animations together; there is no application-level worker or queue.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Not cache-driven. Motion-reduction state suppresses animation, and request/class state gates it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the CSS selectors and widget ownership; relative paint cost is not measured, so no negative regression is established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: GPU/paint cost is platform-dependent, but the change replaces a larger animated box-shadow indicator with the existing smaller input-border animation for the affected configuration rather than adding both animations.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the expensive whole-widget glow is removed, and the remaining progress animation is existing behavior intentionally restored without evidence of increased total rendering cost.

Scenarios.Scenario: Notify the user when a chat session becomes idle after queued work drains or becomes stranded
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Observable chat state transitions schedule the existing 500 ms idle notification check. Only after a qualifying busy-to-idle transition can host focus/toast operations occur; those operations remain behind configuration, focus, completion-time, and delay checks.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Potential host focus and OS toast notification through IHostService after a qualifying idle transition.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one notification sequence per qualifying busy-to-idle completion after the existing debounce and notification deduplication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same notification boundary and scheduling existed; the diff extracts the idle observable into a shared helper without increasing notification cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the request-completion critical path because it is delayed and asynchronous.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Tracking scales with the number of live chat models, one disposable observable/scheduler set per model. Pending queue length reads are O(1).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each model has one RunOnceScheduler; notifications are independently asynchronous and existing dedupe/cancellation state prevents duplicate active notifications for a session.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Observable derivation caches the boolean idle value and only the busy-to-idle delta schedules work; no external cache applies.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that shared-helper behavior matches the deleted implementation and that the external notification boundary is unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneous background sessions varies, but the diff does not add model trackers or external calls.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: this is a behavior-preserving extraction with constant-time reads and unchanged delayed IPC cardinality.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all eight changed files and traced startup, editor-topology telemetry, chat rendering/state updates, queue handling, focus listeners, and notification boundaries. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
